evidence_candidates.claim: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is an amending act for Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 concerning implementation of harmonised AI rules.
qualifiers: The act is dated 8 July 2026 and the Official Journal page identifies publication on 24 July 2026.
uncertainties: Page 1 is marked REVIEW_REQUIRED and needs independent local fidelity review.

evidence_candidates.claim: For Article 6(1) high-risk systems, the act explains that AI Act requirements may be limited where Annex I Section A legislation supplies equivalent protection, provided the AI Act protection level is preserved.
qualifiers: This recital explains the purpose of the operative Article 2(13) amendment on Page 16.

evidence_candidates.claim: The amendment targets the safety-component concept to systems capable of adversely affecting the health and safety of persons or property, because that concept determines part of the Article 6(1) high-risk classification gate.
qualifiers: This is recital-level explanation; the operative definition appears on Page 16 and Article 6 clarifications on Page 18.

evidence_candidates.claim: The act states that Article 5 is amended to address AI systems generating non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material.
qualifiers: This recital gives the legislative rationale; the operative prohibitions appear on Page 18.

evidence_candidates.claim: The recitals distinguish provider and deployer conditions for the new prohibited-content practices and limit the deployer prohibition to purposeful generation or manipulation of the specified material.
qualifiers: Provider conditions turn on intended purpose or a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without adequate safeguards.
uncertainties: The operative wording on Page 18 controls the legal test.

evidence_candidates.claim: The child-sexual-abuse-material prohibition preserves cases covered by a national-law 'without right' defence, including legitimate authority activity and legitimate compliance evaluation described in the recital.
qualifiers: The operative cross-reference is to Directive 2011/93/EU and national law.
uncertainties: Applicability of the national-law defence requires jurisdiction-specific legal review.

evidence_candidates.claim: The act explains that the application dates for Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 are moved to 2 December 2027 for Article 6(2)/Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Article 6(1)/Annex I systems.
qualifiers: This is recital-level explanation; the operative Article 113 amendment appears on Page 35.

evidence_candidates.claim: The act explains that machinery legislation is moved from Annex I Section A to Section B so that the limited Article 2(2) AI Act regime applies to those machines while sector legislation incorporates specified protections.
qualifiers: The operative Annex I amendment appears on Page 36.

evidence_candidates.claim: For Article 6(1) high-risk AI systems related to products under Annex I Section B, amended Article 2(2) limits AI Act application to Article 6(1), Article 60a and Articles 102 to 112.
qualifiers: Articles 57, 58 and 59 apply only where high-risk requirements have been integrated into the relevant harmonisation legislation.

evidence_candidates.claim: Amended Article 2(7) confirms that Union data-protection, privacy and communications-confidentiality law applies to personal data processed in connection with AI Act rights and obligations.
qualifiers: The provision is without prejudice to Articles 4a and 59 and states that the AI Act does not affect the listed data-protection instruments.

evidence_candidates.claim: New Article 2(13) permits specific requirements or obligations in Articles 9 to 15 and 17 to 25 for Article 6(1) systems to be limited only where Annex I Section A legislation provides equivalent or higher protection and the overall AI Act protection level is not reduced.
qualifiers: The concrete systems, requirements, conditions and extent of any limitation depend on delegated acts.

evidence_candidates.claim: The Commission must adopt delegated acts by 2 August 2027 specifying the Article 2(13) high-risk systems and the requirements, conditions and scope of permitted limitations.
qualifiers: The delegation concerns Article 6(1) systems and the limits described in Article 2(13).

evidence_candidates.claim: Amended Article 3(14) defines a safety component by its safety function or by whether its failure or malfunction endangers persons' or property health and safety; a safety function has the intended purpose of preventing or mitigating such risks.
qualifiers: This definition feeds the Article 6(1) high-risk classification gate.

evidence_candidates.claim: Article 5(1)(ba) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service or using an AI system to generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit material of an identifiable natural person without the specified explicit consent.
qualifiers: Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit for the generation or manipulation.

evidence_candidates.claim: Article 5(1)(bb) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service or using an AI system to generate or manipulate material or performance covered by Directive 2011/93/EU, subject to a national-law 'without right' defence.
qualifiers: The provision cross-refers specifically to Article 2(c) and (e) of Directive 2011/93/EU.
uncertainties: The national-law defence requires jurisdiction-specific assessment.

evidence_candidates.claim: For providers, Article 5(1a) applies the new prohibitions where generation or manipulation is the system's intended purpose, or is a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification and adequate preventive and corrective safeguards are absent.
qualifiers: The test considers design, training, architecture, capabilities, user-facing functions and reasonably foreseeable misuse.

evidence_candidates.claim: For deployers, Article 5(1a) applies the new prohibited-content rules only when the system is used for the purpose of generating or manipulating the specified material or performance.
Article 5(1b) excludes from the intimate-material manipulation concept changes that neither increase exposure of depicted intimate parts nor alter the nature of depicted sexually explicit activity.

New Article 6(1a) excludes from the safety-component classification systems used solely for non-safety aspects of user assistance, performance optimisation, service efficiency, automation, convenience or quality control.
qualifiers: The exclusion is limited by Article 6(1b).

evidence_candidates.claim: Article 6(1b) classifies an AI system as a safety component when its failure or malfunction would endanger health and safety, notwithstanding Article 6(1a).
Article 6(1c) states that a product does not satisfy Article 6(1)(b) when third-party conformity assessment is required solely for risks unrelated to health and safety.
qualifiers: The provision gives spectrum distribution and non-health electromagnetic interference as examples.

evidence_candidates.claim: For Annex I Section A products, classification as high-risk under Article 6(1) does not itself remove a conformity-assessment option allowed by the relevant harmonisation legislation or require third-party assessment solely because a high-risk safety component is present.
qualifiers: Any standards-based option remains subject to applying standards or common specifications covering all Chapter III Section 2 requirements.

evidence_candidates.claim: For pre-existing high-risk systems outside Article 111(1), the amended transition rule generally applies the AI Act after the relevant Chapter III date only where the system design is significantly changed from that date.
qualifiers: High-risk systems intended for use by public authorities are subject to a separate compliance deadline of 2 August 2030.

evidence_candidates.claim: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities must take the necessary compliance steps by 2 August 2030.
The new Article 5(1)(ba) and (bb) prohibitions and their Article 5(1a) and (1b) conditions apply from 2 December 2026.
Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 apply from 2 December 2027 to systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III, except Article 6(5).
Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 apply from 2 August 2028 to systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(1) and Annex I, except Article 6(5).
AI Act Articles 102 to 110 apply from 27 July 2026 under the amended Article 113 schedule.
The amendment deletes Annex I Section A point 1 and adds Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery as point 21 of Annex I Section B.
qualifiers: The change alters which AI Act provisions apply to Article 6(1) machinery systems through amended Article 2(2).

evidence_candidates.claim: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 enters into force on the third day following its Official Journal publication and is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
qualifiers: Page 1 identifies the publication date as 24 July 2026; Page 35 separately gives 27 July 2026 for Articles 102 to 110.
uncertainties: Any calendar-date derivation from the publication rule should be independently checked during legal-currentness audit.

unresolved_items: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 does not amend or reproduce the Article 3(1) definition of an AI system; that definition must be supported from the reviewed current AI Act text rather than inferred from this amendment.

This source is an amending act, not a consolidated reproduction of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; full current provisions require deterministic consolidation or a separately ingested authoritative consolidated text.
